html:
The Yanktonai are a division of the Sioux (Očhéthi Šakówiŋ) who speak Dakota and are close kin of the Yankton; together they are often called the Western Dakota. In the 1700s and 1800s they lived in the prairie and lake country of eastern North Dakota and the James River valley, hunting bison and trading at posts on the Missouri. The Assiniboine are thought to have split from them long before. Their divisions included the Hunkpatina, or Lower Yanktonai.

Treaties in the 1860s cut their lands, and they settled on the Standing Rock, Crow Creek, Devils Lake and Fort Peck reservations. Their neighbours were the Lakota to the west and the Sisseton to the east. Earlier maps show them as Yanktonai.
